title: Bounded site comparison of compact-support exchange transposes
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum [def-pur-conventions]: $k$ is an algebraic closure of a finite field of characteristic $p$, $\ell\ne p$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite, $n\ge1$ and $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. All schemes are finite-type $k$-schemes and every morphism to which compact support is applied is separated and finite type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. No absolute separatedness is assumed. For each such $h:S\to T$ choose $c_h=(j_h:S\hookrightarrow\overline S,r_h:\overline S\to T)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. On ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], put $C_V=\nu_V^*$ [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback], $F_h^e=Rr_{h,e,*}j_{h,!}^e$ and $F_h^p=Rr_{h,p,*}j_{h,!}^p$. Use the specified proper-mate/open comparison $B_h:C_TF_h^e\xrightarrow{\sim}F_h^pC_S$ [lem-pur-compact-support-site-coherence], the ordinary etale right adjoint $G_h^e$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], the transported $G_h^p=Rh^!$ [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and their counits $\varepsilon_h^e,\varepsilon_h^p$. Write $a_{h,L}=\rho_L:C_SG_h^eL\xrightarrow{\sim}G_h^pC_TL$ for the comparison induced by the site-adjunction unit, with the bounded-origin Hom normalization of [lem-pur-bounded-site-adjunction-transpose]. Only bounded-below etale inputs, bounded-below exceptional images, and bounded-below intermediate etale objects of the displayed composites are used; all pro-etale exceptional Hom bijections are the bounded etale-origin ones.

Let $f:X\to Y$ and let $v:Y'\to Y$ be any morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes. Put $X'=X\times_YY'$, $w:X'\to X$, $f':X'\to Y'$ and use the pulled-back compactification $c'$ [def-cbc-compact-support-square]. Use the canonical comparison-pullback identifications [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. Write
$$E^e:v_e^*F_f^e\to F_{f'}^ew_e^*,\qquad E^p:v_p^*F_f^p\to F_{f'}^pw_p^*$$
for the actual chosen-compactification exchanges [def-cbc-exchange-map, def-exchange-projection], namely the proper unit--square--counit exchange followed by open extension-by-zero base change. Their components on bounded-below etale inputs and their comparison images are isomorphisms. For bounded-below $K$ with the required bounded-below exceptional images, define
$$d^\sigma_K:w_\sigma^*G_f^\sigma K\longrightarrow G_{f'}^\sigma v_\sigma^*K$$
to be the specified adjoint transpose under $F_{f'}^\sigma\dashv G_{f'}^\sigma$ of
$$F_{f'}^\sigma w_\sigma^*G_f^\sigma K\xrightarrow{(E^\sigma_{G_f^\sigma K})^{-1}}v_\sigma^*F_f^\sigma G_f^\sigma K\xrightarrow{v_\sigma^*\varepsilon^\sigma_{f,K}}v_\sigma^*K.$$
Here $d^p$ is evaluated at $C_YK$. Under the canonical pullback identifications, the following equality holds:
$$a_{f',v_e^*K}\circ C_{X'}(d^e_K)
=d^p_{C_YK}\circ w_p^*(a_{f,K}).$$
At $K=A_Y$, including $v^*A_Y\cong A_{Y'}$, this identifies the actual dualizing base-change arrows of [def-pur-co-smoothness]. It does not assert that these exceptional arrows are invertible. The same comparison identifies the mates of the forward exchanges under any of the specified adjunctions for which those mates are defined [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. These equalities preserve identity squares, horizontal and vertical Cartesian pasting, proper refinement, and further compatible open restriction, on exactly the bounded etale-origin domains stated above. No separatedness, properness or smoothness of $v$ is assumed, and no exceptional adjunction on all unbounded pro-etale inputs is asserted.

proof.text:
The finite-setting lemma [lem-pur-finite-setting-comparison-hypotheses] supplies finiteness of $A$, finite-dimensional bounds for each chosen compactification and its base changes, including empty sources. Thus [lem-pur-bounded-site-adjunction-transpose] applies to $f,f'$ on the bounded domains in the statement. Suppress only the canonical pullback identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. For every bounded-below $M$, [lem-pur-co-smooth-exchange-transport] gives the equality of the actual maps
$$E^p_{C_XM}\,v_p^*B_{f,M}=B_{f',w_e^*M}\,C_{Y'}(E^e_M). \tag{1}$$
The $B$ here are exactly the proper-counit-mate/open comparisons specified in the item. The etale exchange is invertible by [thm-cbc-finite-torsion]; (1) and invertibility of $B$ give invertibility of the pro-etale exchange on comparison inputs. Inverting (1) gives
$$(E^p_{C_XM})^{-1}B_{f',w_e^*M}=v_p^*B_{f,M}\,C_{Y'}((E^e_M)^{-1}). \tag{2}$$

source.place: Tag 0B65, lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints, counit normalization; agent application to the bounded-origin Hom bijections and the specified compactification exchanges.

proof.text:
Set $M=G_f^eK$, $J=w_e^*M$, $H=v_e^*K$ and $a=a_{f,K}$. These objects and all intervening etale objects are bounded below by the bounded-below hypotheses stated above. The counit normalization in [lem-pur-bounded-site-adjunction-transpose] says precisely
$$\varepsilon^p_{f,C_YK}\,F_f^p(a)\,B_{f,M}=C_Y(\varepsilon^e_{f,K}). \tag{3}$$
Write $q_e=v_e^*(\varepsilon^e_{f,K})(E^e_M)^{-1}$ and $q_p=v_p^*(\varepsilon^p_{f,C_YK})(E^p_{G_f^pC_YK})^{-1}$. These are the untransposed arrows defining $d^e_K,d^p_{C_YK}$, respectively. They are actual counit composites, rather than arbitrary arrows between their endpoints.

source.place: Tag 0B65, lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints, counit normalization; agent application to the bounded-origin Hom bijections and the specified compactification exchanges.

proof.text:
Naturality of the actual pro-etale exchange in the isomorphism $a:C_XM\to G_f^pC_YK$ gives
$$(E^p_{G_f^pC_YK})^{-1}F_{f'}^p(w_p^*a)=v_p^*F_f^p(a)(E^p_{C_XM})^{-1}.$$
Consequently the following is an equality of arrows $C_{Y'}F_{f'}^eJ\to C_{Y'}H$:
$$\begin{aligned}
q_p F_{f'}^p(w_p^*a)B_{f',J}
&=v_p^*(\varepsilon^p_{f,C_YK}F_f^p(a))(E^p_{C_XM})^{-1}B_{f',J}\\
&=v_p^*(\varepsilon^p_{f,C_YK}F_f^p(a)B_{f,M})C_{Y'}((E^e_M)^{-1})\\
&=C_{Y'}(v_e^*\varepsilon^e_{f,K})C_{Y'}((E^e_M)^{-1})
=C_{Y'}(q_e).
\end{aligned} \tag{4}$$
The successive equalities use naturality, (2), and (3), respectively; the pullback-comparison naturality of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] identifies the third line. Before suppressing identifications, insert $F_{f'}^p(\kappa_{w,M})$ immediately before $B_{f',J}$ and $\kappa_{v,K}^{-1}$ immediately after $q_p$, where $\kappa_u:C u_e^*\cong u_p^*C$. Thus (4) has exactly the required source and target.

proof.text:
Apply the transpose comparison [lem-pur-bounded-site-adjunction-transpose] for $f'$ to $q_e$ and the arrow $q_pF_{f'}^p(w_p^*a)$ (with the identifications of (4)). Equation (4) is precisely its compatibility hypothesis. Its conclusion identifies the pro-etale transpose with $a_{f',H}C_{X'}(\operatorname{adj}_e(q_e))$. Source naturality of the same specified Hom bijection identifies that pro-etale transpose with $\operatorname{adj}_p(q_p)w_p^*a$. By the definitions of $d^e,d^p$, this is the claimed equality
$$a_{f',v_e^*K}C_{X'}(d^e_K)=d^p_{C_YK}w_p^*(a_{f,K}).$$
Only the bounded-origin Hom bijection for $f'$ was used: its source is witnessed by $J$, and the witness is changed by the displayed isomorphism $w_p^*a$.

proof.text: Take $K=A_Y$. Inverse image of a constant coefficient sheaf is the constant coefficient sheaf: the constant-sheaf functor is inverse image from the point, and composition of inverse images gives $v^*A_Y\cong A_{Y'}$ and $C_YA_Y\cong A_Y$ on the pro-etale site. Condition (3) in [def-pur-co-smoothness] defines its dualizing arrow as the $Rf'_!\dashv Rf'^!$ transpose of the inverse of the transported pro-etale exchange at $\omega_f=Rf^!A_Y$, followed by pullback of the counit and this constant-sheaf identification. The object $\omega_f$ has the etale-origin witness $(f^\times A_Y,a_{f,A_Y})$, and the transport clause of [lem-pur-co-smooth-exchange-transport] identifies the transported exchange at a witnessed input with the specified pro-etale compactification composite $E^p$, independently of the witness. Hence that dualizing arrow is $d^p_{C_YA_Y}$ composed with the constant-sheaf identifications, and Step 4 identifies those named dualizing arrows. No inversion of $d^e$ or $d^p$ occurs; in particular invertibility of $E$ has not been mistaken for invertibility of its exceptional mate.

proof.text: For forward exchanges and any of the specified available adjunctions, use the mate formula of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. A mate is the composite of a unit, the given square, and a counit. Under site comparison its middle square is (1). For an exceptional adjunction its unit and counit are compared by the specified Hom normalization of [lem-pur-bounded-site-adjunction-transpose] (the unit is the transpose of the identity); for inverse-image/direct-image adjunctions the counit-mate normalization is [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate], with pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. Regard $B$, the pullback comparisons and the direct-image comparisons as squares between the etale and pro-etale adjunctions, with $C$ on both sides; (1) is then an equality of two pasted squares. Clauses 1 and 2 of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] turn it into the equality of the pasted mates, the mate of each comparison square being the right-adjoint comparison just named, and clause 3 inserts the identifications $\kappa$ and the inverses of the invertible comparisons at the boundaries. This identifies the resulting mates. This proves comparison of the actual forward mates wherever all their adjunctions and intermediate objects have the stated domains. It asserts neither that taking a general mate preserves invertibility nor an exceptional adjunction outside those domains.

source.place: Tag 0B65, lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints, counit normalization; agent application to the bounded-origin Hom bijections and the specified compactification exchanges.

proof.text: For identity squares, [thm-cbc-finite-torsion] gives identity exchanges, and clause 4 of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] gives identity mates. For either Cartesian pasting, that theorem identifies the etale exchange of the rectangle with the pasted exchanges; the pullback compositors agree under site comparison by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. Inverting a composite reverses its factors. Apply clauses 1 and 2 of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] to these factors: their mates are the corresponding pasted exceptional arrows, with the composite adjunction's counit, so Steps 3--4 identify both assemblies with the same transpose. For forward mates apply the same clauses without inversion. For proper refinement, [thm-cbc-finite-torsion] identifies the exchanges under refinement, while [lem-pur-compact-support-site-coherence] identifies $B$ under refinement and compact-support composition. Clause 3 of the mate-pasting lemma then inserts exactly the conjugate refinement/composition maps on the right adjoints. For further compatible open restriction, the open restriction square for $B$ in that coherence lemma and the base-change pasting law just used give the same argument after appending the open Cartesian square. Thus each asserted equality survives all the stated operations. Every application is to a finite displayed composite with bounded-below etale intermediates as required, and none imposes any extra property on $v$.
